messages.subject: Packrat bundle project folder + Jenkins
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using packrat to automatic bundle packages via Jenkins... e.g. Jenkins automatically checksout any changes in my R projects, makes a few tests and then runs packrat and bundles the projects so they can deployed automatically.
No my problem is the folder name... currently for whateverGIT (HUB) related reason, jenkins puts my projects in folders with some huge suffix,e.g.:

myproject becomes myproject-4IPDUOECNJZOZAE4OCUREGBUEOUZ6EAZWXNUQCCROBBXHSU2FXYA

While I can change the name of the zip back (and packrat::bundle supports such an option) - I couldnt find a way to make packrat not include this long folder. This leads to problems too with gzip/tar as the name is too long for some files:
 In tar(tarfile = file, files = basename(project), compression = "gzip",  :
  storing paths of more than 100 bytes is not portable:
  'myproject-4IPDUOECNJZOZAE4OCUREGBUEOUZ6EAZWXNUQCCROBBXHSU2FXYA/packrat/packrat.lock'

Are there any workarounds? Some ugly ideas I had.
Just don't use packrat bundle but any zip client
Copy all files in the correct subfolder first and then run packrat
Ideally, it should be possible to specify the folder name... or packrat is packing the folder content... the folder itself can still be created when unbundling.

messages.subject: Re: Packrat bundle project folder + Jenkins
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

Packrat does try to preserve the folder name during 'bundle()', so I think exploring one of your workarounds is likely the best bet here (and I think both would work fine).

Ultimately, all 'bundle()' does it try to create a tarball of the files in your project, with a bit of extra work done to ensure that e.g. 'packrat/src', 'packrat/lib' and some other folders are not included in the tarball. Unfortunately, it's not currently possible to allow for user-supplied filters in selecting what is, or isn't, included.

Thanks,
Kevin
